conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my three children.

I have Alex who is 21, Blake who is 15, and Charlie who is 11.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me gather a few more details about each of your children to assess your eligibility.

Starting with **Alex (age 21)**: Is Alex currently in approved education or training, such as A-levels, a vocational qualification (up to NVQ level 3), or an unpaid apprenticeship? And do they live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me anymore - they moved out. And no, they're not in any education or training. They actually work full-time now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying about Alex.

Now, let me ask about **Blake (age 15)**: Does Blake live with you? And are they currently in full-time education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Blake doesn't live with me either. Blake lives with their other parent. I do help out a bit financially when I can - I send some money for things they need.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Blake. Even though Blake doesn't live with you, there may still be some circumstances where you could claim, so I have a couple of follow-up questions.

Regarding **Blake**: Do you contribute at least the same amount towards Blake's upkeep as the Child Benefit would be worth (currently £25.60 per week for a first/only child, or £16.95 for additional children)? And is Blake's other parent (or anyone else Blake lives with) already claiming Child Benefit for them?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I send about £10 a week when I can manage it - so no, it's not as much as the Child Benefit amount. And yes, their other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for Blake.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for those details about Blake.

Now let me ask about **Charlie (age 11)**: Does Charlie live with you? And are they currently in full-time education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Charlie lives with me at home. And yes, they're in school - they're in Year 6.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for each of your three children.

Let me just confirm one more detail: Are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to make an assessment for each of your children.

conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, here is my assessment of your Child Benefit eligibility:

---

### **Alex (age 21)** — ❌ Not Eligible
Alex is 21 years old and working full-time. Child Benefit is only available for children under 16, or for those aged 16-19 who remain in approved education or training. Since Alex is over 20 and not in approved education or training, you cannot claim Child Benefit for them.

---

### **Blake (age 15)** — ❌ Not Eligible
Although Blake is under 16, they don't live with you. To claim Child Benefit for a child who lives with someone else, you would need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment towards their upkeep (£25.60/week for a first child, or £16.95/week for additional children). Your contribution of around £10 per week is below this threshold. Additionally, Blake's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for Blake, and only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child.

---

### **Charlie (age 11)** — ✅ Eligible
Great news! Charlie is under 16, lives with you, is in full-time education, and you live in the UK. You meet all the eligibility requirements and can claim Child Benefit for Charlie.

---

### Summary
You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for **Charlie** only. If you haven't already, you can make a claim through the Child Benefit Office.

Is there anything else you'd like to know?
